issue_title: Archive finished projects instead of deleting them
issue_body:
Deleting a finished project today removes it outright, and its history goes with it.

Add `POST /projects/{id}/archive`. A project admin may archive a project: the call returns `200` with the project and sets its `archived_at`. Any other caller gets `403`, and an unknown project id gets `404`. An archived project no longer appears in `GET /projects`, but it stays readable by its members: `GET /projects/{id}` keeps returning `200` with the project for a member.

plan.summary: Add an admin-only archive endpoint that stamps archived_at and hides archived projects from the project list.

approach.description: Add migration 0021 adding a nullable archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ column to projects, with a down migration dropping it.
Add ArchiveProject to internal/store/projects.go (UPDATE projects SET archived_at = now()), and add archived_at IS NULL to the projectVisible predicate that ListProjects and GetProject share.
Add the POST /projects/{id}/archive handler: load the project (404 when unknown), require the project admin role (403 otherwise), call ArchiveProject and return 200 with the project.
Document POST /projects/{id}/archive and its 403 and 404 responses in api/openapi.yaml.

verification.test_strategy: Handler tests: an admin archive returns 200 and stamps archived_at, a non-admin gets 403, an unknown id gets 404, and the list and detail reads are asserted after archiving. A store test covers ArchiveProject.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR and run the 0021 down migration; archived_at values are dropped and archived projects reappear in the list.

acceptance_criteria.statement: POST /projects/{id}/archive by a project admin returns HTTP 200 with the project, sets archived_at on the project, drops the project from GET /projects for every caller, and afterwards a member's GET /projects/{id} returns HTTP 404.
POST /projects/{id}/archive by a member who is not a project admin returns HTTP 403 and leaves archived_at unset.
POST /projects/{id}/archive for an unknown project id returns HTTP 404.
GET /projects still lists every project of the caller whose archived_at is unset.

risks_and_assumptions: Project admin is the existing role checked by the settings endpoints.

catch_probes: hides the project from its members

catching_examples.note: ac-archive-by-admin contradicts the issue: an archived project stays readable by its members, so a member's GET /projects/{id} must return 200, not 404.

ac-archive-by-admin bundles correct clauses with a last one that requires the opposite of the issue: after archiving, members lose read access, while the issue keeps GET /projects/{id} returning 200 for them. Approach step 2's shared projectVisible predicate produces the same 404.

The criterion that drops the project from GET /projects for every caller also expects a member's GET /projects/{id} to return 404 afterwards; members can still read an archived project per the issue, so it should return 200 rather than 404.

Criterion ac-archive-by-admin is mostly right (200, archived_at, hidden from the list), but its final clause directly contradicts the issue it cites: the issue says an archived project stays readable by its members and GET /projects/{id} keeps returning 200 for a member. Approach step 2 adds archived_at IS NULL to the predicate GetProject shares, so the implementation would follow the wrong clause. Split the criterion and expect 200 for a member's detail read.

non_catching_examples.note: No test archives a project that is already archived; decide whether a second archive returns 200 again or 409.
Adding archived_at IS NULL to every project query needs a partial index, or GET /projects slows down as archived projects pile up.
ac-archive-by-admin should also assert that the archive response body carries the archived_at timestamp.
ac-archive-by-admin is ambiguous about whose clock stamps archived_at; a mismatch between the database clock and the test clock makes the assertion flaky.
Document POST /projects/{id}/archive and its 403 and 404 responses in api/openapi.yaml.
ac-archive-non-admin-403: a member who is not a project admin gets 403; also test a caller who is not a member at all.
An archived project no longer appears in GET /projects; the plan has no way for an admin to list archived projects to restore one.
